lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: The Owl Who Was Afraid of the Dark
lesson.summary: Read and talk about a story where a little owl learns that the dark can be kind.
lesson.unit: Topic 9: The Owl Who Was Afraid of the Dark
learning_objectives: Explain the theme of facing a fear

standards.text: Discuss characters, settings and events; make predictions; draw inferences about feelings; link a story's theme to our own lives

success_criteria: I can name the character and setting
I can use clues to predict
I can say how the dark can be kind
lesson.real_life: Night skies in Lahore and the Lake District, bedtime duas, and calm night routines.

blocks.title: Omar and the night light
blocks.transcript: It is bedtime. Omar's night light flickers. The room goes dark. Omar feels a little scared. He thinks of Plop, the owl afraid of the dark. Plop met kind people. They showed him good things about the dark. Omar looks at the window. He sees the stars. He takes a slow, deep breath. He says a bedtime dua. The dark feels soft and cosy. He is not afraid. Omar sleeps. The dark can be kind, just like Plop learned.
blocks.caption: Omar thinks of Plop when his night light flickers.

points: Plop is a baby barn owl
His problem is that he fears the dark

blocks.text: Stop 1: Plan a fear and a fix

blocks.say: Now we make our own story. Every story has a problem and a fix.

blocks.markdown: Nights in Lahore can feel dark and long.
blocks.say: In Pakistan, some children feel nervous in a power cut. Candles can help.

blocks.markdown: Winter nights in the Lake District are long.
blocks.say: In the UK, some children feel nervous when the clocks go back. Winter nights come early.

blocks.markdown: Calm routines help us feel safe.
blocks.say: Many families say a bedtime dua. It helps them feel calm and safe.
